incident-bot: P1 — <@eng-runtime> GPU node pool 'infer-pool-3' reporting repeated cudaErrorMemoryAllocation on model-serving containers. 40% of requests to /v1/generate failing with 500; error pattern looks like OOM despite ~20% reported headroom. Paging to #incidents and paging oncall.
Anika (oncall): I'm up. I saw the page, joining. Which cluster/region?
incident-bot: Region: us-west2, nodes: g4dn-16xlarge style. Affected deployment: redwood/model-13b-v2 replicas on node group infer-pool-3. First failure at 1744501208.
Jamie (SRE): I can grab the nodes. nvidia-smi on one node shows GPU mem 0/128Gi reported as used ~105Gi for a few processes but allocator reports fragmentation when larger contiguous alloc requested. Kernel logs attached: `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory` and `CUDACachingAllocator: Allocation of size 536870912 failed` repeatedly.
Kevin (eng-runtime): Thanks. This matches a fragmentation pattern we've seen when the caching allocator reserves many small blocks and later big allocations fail. We should check if `cudaMallocAsync` is enabled and whether the runtime reserved block size has drifted. Also check for pinned host allocations that can pressure device.
Anika (oncall): What's customer impact? Maria?
Maria (prod-support): Currently ~12 customer requests per minute hitting 500s across two customers on dedicated capacity (cust-A, cust-B). We've opened tickets and flagged SEV for cust-A. No external status page update yet.
Lee (eng-ml): Model-level note: the model variant uses large KV cache and occasional long-prefix requests cause big spike in contiguous allocation. If cache gets fragmented by many smaller requests, that can cause later allocs to fail even if free memory sum > allocation size.
Jamie (SRE): I'm SSHing to node infer-3a-7. Running `pmap`-like memory check in container and host. Command I ran: 
```
kubectl -n serve exec -it model-13b-v2-rr7 -- bash -c "python -c 'import torch; print(torch.cuda.memory_summary())'"
```
Output shows many small cached blocks and peak_allocations > current_allocations.
Kevin (eng-runtime): Immediate mitigation options: 1) restart problematic container to clear CUDACachingAllocator caches 2) drain node and cordon to let workloads move 3) enable fallback to smaller model-variant for new requests 4) reduce per-replica concurrency / max_batch_size to lower allocation spikes.
Anika (oncall): Which one we do first? I can kill & restart the container now.
Jamie (SRE): Restarting the container will be quickest. Do a graceful restart via the rollout API so it drains requests and then kills. I'm going to cordon node after restart.
Anika (oncall): Doing restart now for model-13b-v2-rr7 on infer-3a-7. `kubectl -n serve rollout restart deployment/model-13b-v2 --selector=pod=model-13b-v2-rr7` (using safe restart script).
deploy-bot: Deploy restart initiated by Anika (oncall) for deployment model-13b-v2. Rollout started: 2/6 updated.
Jamie (SRE): After restart, I see freed memory on that GPU; nvidia-smi shows GPU free now ~60Gi. But another pod on same node failed to allocate soon after. This indicates fragmentation across multiple pods on same GPU card due to shared allocator arena.
Kevin (eng-runtime): We're running with shared GPU multi-tenant scheduling. For now, immediately lower `MAX_CONCURRENCY` for the deployment to 1 and reduce `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS` to 128 to reduce peak contiguous alloc sizes. I'll patch the config.
Anika (oncall): Patch applied — concurrency -> 1, batch tokens -> 128. Monitoring for failures.
Maria (prod-support): After restart + config change, errors dropped to near zero for 10 minutes for cust-A; cust-B still saw intermittent 500s but reduced. I've messaged both customers: cust-A not impacted anymore, cust-B asked for ETA.
Lee (eng-ml): For longer term: we should consider 1) forcing periodic `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` after long prefix evictions in the runtime 2) experimenting with `cudaMallocAsync` vs legacy allocator to reduce fragmentation 3) reserve a contiguous block per replica at startup (headroom reservation) to avoid fragmentation-induced failures.
Kevin (eng-runtime): Agree. Also adding a temporary per-node restart policy: if `CUDACachingAllocator` fails X times within Y seconds, automatically restart the offending pod and mark node for deeper diagnosis. I'll file a patch.
Jamie (SRE): Node-level mitigation: cordon infer-3a-7 and drain other pods off it to stop further fragmentation while we investigate. I've cordoned it.
Anika (oncall): Cordoned node infer-3a-7. Ongoing monitoring. Are there any crash loops?
Jamie (SRE): One container entered CrashLoopBackOff yesterday after unusual large prefix request; logs show repeated `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation`. We'll capture that container's heap map and upload to S3 for offline analysis.
Kevin (eng-runtime): For quick debugging, can we get the output of `torch.cuda.memory_reserved()` vs `torch.cuda.memory_allocated()` from the runtime metrics per process? We should log these for failed requests. I'll add temporary metrics.
Lee (eng-ml): Also check the driver/CUDA version — we've seen fragmentation regressions in CUDA 11.8 with certain kernels. What driver version are nodes running?
Jamie (SRE): Nodes: NVIDIA driver 535.54, CUDA 12.1 runtime. I've opened a ticket with infra to check known issues.
Maria (prod-support): Customer comms: cust-A closed their SEV, cust-B escalated to account team but accepted current mitigations. I drafted a status update for impacted customers explaining transient OOM due to allocator fragmentation and temporary mitigations (restarts, reduced concurrency). Want approval before posting.
Anika (oncall): Approve the customer-facing wording but add "we are investigating root cause and will follow up with a plan to avoid recurrence".
Kevin (eng-runtime): Post-incident next steps I'm assigning: 1) Add guardrails to detect fragmentation patterns and auto-fallback (ENG-RT-423) 2) Evaluate allocator settings and reserved contiguous headroom per replica (ENG-RT-424) 3) Add per-request memory diagnostics to logs for failed alloc ops (ENG-RT-425). I'll own 1 & 2.
Jamie (SRE): I'll own node-level remediation playbook and add it to runbook (SRE-221).
Lee (eng-ml): I'll run a repro harness that simulates long-prefix + many small requests to reproduce fragmentation locally.
Anika (oncall): Current status: errors down, node cordoned, container restarts & config change in flight. Closing page in 30m if stable.
incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged by oncall: Anika. Notes: 12 errors/min peak, primary mitigation: restart pods + reduce concurrency, cordon node infer-3a-7. Tags: gpu, cuda, oom, fragmentation, serving-runtime.
Maria (prod-support): Final customer note posted to cust-A and cust-B. Closing ticket for cust-A. Cust-B will remain open until ENG-RT patch.
Anika (oncall): Marking as mitigated. Will hand off to Kevin & Jamie for RCA. Oncall out at 1744501300.
Kevin (eng-runtime): Logging followup plan in tracker and will schedule a postmortem with timeline.
Jamie (SRE): Uploading logs and memory dumps to S3: s3://redwood-incidents/1744501234/.
Lee (eng-ml): Repro harness started. Will share results in #eng-ml tomorrow.
Anika (oncall): Thanks all, good job. :thumbsup:
